en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not sever ties with one another, and be, O servants of Allah, brothers.' 'Ali ibn Nasr al-Jahdami narrated it to me: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, and he added: 'as Allah has commanded you.'

Abu Kamil narrated to us: Yazid—meaning Ibn Zuray'—narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated to us from 'Abd al-Razzaq; all of them from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission. As for the narration of Yazid from him, it is like the narration of Sufyan from al-Zuhri, mentioning all four traits; and as for the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 'and do not envy one another, do not sever ties with one another, and do not turn your backs on one another.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ibn Abi 'Umar, and 'Amr al-Naqid all narrated to us from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, and Ibn 'Uyaynah added: 'and do not sever ties with one another.'

Hajib ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Zubaydi narrated to us, from al-Zuhri: Anas ibn Malik informed me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said; (H) and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated it to me: Ibn Wahb informed me: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the like of the hadith of Malik.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us; he said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be, O servants of Allah, brothers. And it is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three [days].'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna; they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrating from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have relatives with whom I try to maintain ties, but they sever them; I treat them well, but they treat me badly; I am forbearing with them, but they act ignorantly toward me.' He said: 'If you are as you say, it is as if you are feeding them hot ashes, and you will not cease to have a supporter from Allah against them so long as you remain upon that.'

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather: 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me; he said: Ibn Shihab said: Anas ibn Malik informed me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Whoever loves that his provision be expanded for him and his lifespan be prolonged, let him maintain the ties of kinship.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'Whoever would be pleased to have his provision expanded for him or his lifespan prolonged, let him maintain the ties of kinship.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, and he said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).'

'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma' al-Duba'i narrated to me: Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, that Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed him that his father informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'One who severs the ties of kinship will not enter Paradise.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to me; they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'A severer will not enter Paradise.' Ibn Abi 'Umar said: Sufyan said: meaning a severer of ties of kinship.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's; they said: Waki' narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The womb (kinship) is suspended from the Throne, saying: "Whoever maintains ties with me, Allah maintains ties with him; and whoever severs ties with me, Allah severs ties with him."'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id ibn Jamil ibn Tarif ibn 'Abdullah al-Thaqafi and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us; they said: Hatim—who is Ibn Isma'il—narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah—who is Ibn Abi Muzarrid, the freed slave of Banu Hashim: my uncle Abu al-Hubab Sa'id ibn Yasar narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, Allah created the creation until, when He finished with them, the womb (kinship) stood up and said: "This is the station of the seeker of refuge with You from being severed." He said: "Yes. Are you not satisfied that I maintain ties with whoever maintains ties with you, and sever ties with whoever severs ties with you?" She said: "Yes, indeed." He said: "Then that is yours."' Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Recite if you wish: {So would you perhaps, if you turned away, cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship? Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He deafened them and blinded their vision. Do they not then reflect upon the Quran, or are there locks upon their hearts?}'

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Mu'awiyah—meaning Ibn Salih—narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from Nawwas ibn Sim'an, who said: I stayed with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in Medina for a year, nothing preventing me from migrating except the desire to ask questions, for when one of us migrated, he would not ask the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about anything. He said: So I asked him about righteousness and sin, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which wavers in your soul and you would dislike that people should find out about it.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to me: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Ansari, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about righteousness and sin, and he said: 'Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which wavers in your chest and you would dislike that people should find out about it.'

Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father and al-Layth ibn Sa'd both narrated to us, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn Usamah ibn al-Had, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, that whenever he set out for Mecca, he had a donkey on which he would rest when he grew weary of riding the camel, and a turban with which he bound his head. While he was one day upon that donkey, a bedouin passed by him, so he said: 'Are you not the son of so-and-so, son of so-and-so?' He said: 'Yes, indeed.' So he gave him the donkey and said: 'Ride this,' and of the turban he said: 'Bind your head with it.' Some of his companions said to him: 'May Allah forgive you! You gave this bedouin a donkey on which you used to take rest, and a turban with which you used to bind your head.' He said: 'Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Among the greatest acts of righteousness is that a man maintain ties with the family of his father's friend after he has passed away," and his father was indeed a friend of 'Umar.'

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Haywah ibn Shurayh informed me, from Ibn al-Had, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The most dutiful form of righteousness is that a man maintains ties with the friends of his father.'

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub informed me, from al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that a man from among the bedouins met him on the way to Mecca, so 'Abdullah greeted him with peace, mounted him upon a donkey he had been riding, and gave him a turban that had been on his head. Ibn Dinar said: So we said to him: 'May Allah make you prosper! They are bedouins and they are content with little.' Thereupon 'Abdullah said: 'Indeed, this man's father was a friend of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Indeed, the most dutiful form of righteousness is for the son to maintain ties with the family of his father's friend."'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal: Suhayl narrated to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'May his nose be rubbed in the dust,' three times; then he mentioned the like of it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'May his nose be rubbed in the dust, then may his nose be rubbed in the dust, then may his nose be rubbed in the dust!' It was said: 'Who, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'He who finds his parents in their old age, one of them or both of them, and then does not enter Paradise.'

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'May the nose be rubbed in the dust, then may the nose be rubbed in the dust, then may the nose be rubbed in the dust!' It was said: 'Who, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'He who finds his parents in their old age, one of them or both of them, yet does not enter Paradise.'
